b612abfc8faa1bf2937f798235767cb5c2cd8264.sourceText: 1. Introduction: The Politics of Transnational Chinese Correspondence

b8fab63d320c516a72e6cc5464a784a797227fae.sourceText: This research explores the intersection of cultural heritage, interactive design, and embodied experience to transform static historical Chinese diaspora correspondence into dynamic, living encounters. Focusing on

7f4c1a72c19007ecbdd22b4d26ce5f5c63e33db1.sourceText: (侨批) or “letters home” held in the National Museum of Singapore’s collection, we address a fundamental challenge in cultural heritage presentation: how to make historical correspondence emotionally resonant with contemporary audiences while challenging dominant interpretive frameworks.

3dbed3318cf408fb7c26f0b9bd1c160c9f9fe3e1.sourceText: —remittance letters sent by overseas Chinese to their families from the 19th to mid-20th centuries—were recognised by UNESCO as Memory of the World in 2013, acknowledging their significance as crucial lifelines connecting diaspora communities with their families in China (UNESCO, 2013). Despite this recognition, a comprehensive review of existing research reveals significant gaps, particularly regarding marginalised voices and innovative presentation methods.

6ee5a981ad236cbf014fecc5b0a12c15016eac0c.sourceText: 1.1 Dominant Narratives: Nationalism and Historical Contextualisation

922c014a9a528df4e48cf891f97397e99673f1b9.sourceText: A significant body of scholarship positions

e2dd6e4c7ac98400bff77ca999480611c56e5852.sourceText: within nationalist frameworks that emphasise patriotic loyalty to the Chinese motherland. This instrumentalisation is evident in both academic literature and museum presentations, creating what Wang (2019) describes as patriotic educational tools through the display of

1799dc330004fab59987433e11bd494d8b670b55.sourceText: This state-sanctioned narrative prioritises content demonstrating how “overseas Chinese elevated their love for family, clan, and hometown to love for their motherland” (Bai, 2018, p. 131).

5bcff96b5bfb6d9cbe0d29a86b9b95694ad8162b.sourceText: as materials for promoting “traditional Chinese virtues such as patriotism” and conducting “patriotic education.”

60d9ab45014d3d4277b4618d55327bf3be83baac.sourceText: Similarly, Lin and Huang (2020) document how

dd9ca0e91e7884383941a0b8704da641f28cba72.sourceText: are used in education to cultivate “patriotic sentiments” through historical stories related to “loving the party and country.”

1c95b0c02af4ab401b86518bf0f1667f1e3b8a25.sourceText: Historical contextualisation studies frequently reinforce these nationalist frameworks. Zheng (2019) frames

0beebcb001991e39367666f0cb539bb1ffb9c939.sourceText: as evidence of how overseas Chinese “threw themselves into revolutionary activities and anti-Japanese resistance movements.”

a64b85940cd8ff3d94fc1050ef2254ed1110404e.sourceText: Chen and Cen (2021) analyse patriotic sentiments in family correspondence during the war against Japan, showing how resistance to Japanese aggression strengthened cultural identification with China. This historical contextualisation extends to earlier periods as well, with Bai (2018) documenting overseas Chinese involvement in the 1911 Revolution.

a3f47eda7e529189b67ceb7bd9b7d056629d49b1.sourceText: While patriotic sentiments may indeed appear in some correspondences, particularly during periods of national crisis, this dominant interpretive framework risks creating a monolithic narrative that filters overseas Chinese experiences primarily through the lens of state interests. The focus on nationalist themes overshadows the transnational nature of these communications, where identities were negotiated across borders rather than simply affirming singular national allegiances.

4f29201f6ff558f8cda4284efe00a2751b77bb65.sourceText: Scholarship examining the institutional infrastructure of

6635e305648bcf11ef9fee1c9d0c697e7cd92384.sourceText: ) and their transnational banking networks. Dai (2003) pioneered research on these networked enterprises, analysing how they operated within embedded social structures, while his subsequent work examined the transition between traditional and modern business systems as

80a0d1f002072076905c485f6857a4d05756d027.sourceText: developed relationships with formal banking institutions (Dai, 2004). Building on this foundation, Jiao (2010) explored the construction and operation of transnational commercial networks, particularly in Fujian.

d9ba59d1a0f0f4a3b0a4851d6ab14f8912d1a312.sourceText: Western scholarship has similarly recognised these sophisticated financial mechanisms. Harris (2013) analysed “the organisational structure and business practices of Qiaopiju” (p. 130), demonstrating how these firms adapted to emerging regulatory regimes across borders. Benton and Liu (2018) dedicate entire chapters in their book

0a726de834378fc8c8597b3daaf53b5ff5a39fc6.sourceText: to examining “The Structure of Qiaopi Trade and Transnational Networks” and “The Qiaopi Trade as a Distinctive Form of Chinese Capitalism.” Their work represents the first book-length study in English of the origins, structure, and operations of the

00edfd970e9c294ef79920ef10f8a537e33a45e4.sourceText: A significant strand of research examines how

79f79cd594c7805abacc260c4c1041b3ca1c99f6.sourceText: embodied traditional Chinese values, particularly concepts of trust and familial responsibility that sustained remittance networks without formal legal protections. Niu (2013) demonstrates how traditional Confucian moral principles of “benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness”

8b763c0156599239f7575451895c4388222c5aa5.sourceText: permeate these archives, extending their significance beyond mere economic transactions. Li et al. (2023) further this analysis by examining how “trust culture”

fe770510742ad2c16465e04aa8b75d1cdf0186e4.sourceText: functioned across personal, industry, and national levels. These studies consistently highlight how Confucian values of filial piety motivated the maintenance of transnational connections (Deng, 2009).

1747ddcf2d7c77594e58cd9b214622e8ffe83e2c.sourceText: largely reflects historical gender imbalances in overseas Chinese communities. Tian and Xiao (2015) examines letters between male family members, while Zhou (2020) quantifies this gender disparity, documenting that Singapore’s 1931 Hainanese community had a gender ratio of 1000:151 (male:female). This predominant focus on male perspectives has marginalised women’s voices and experiences in both the historical record and subsequent scholarly analysis.

e05db708e8a5450e473c3e70474c19bed86befaf.sourceText: 1.4 The Critical Gap: Marginalised Hainanese Women’s Voices

b04bc1aa56de5f8c06ed5be4ac04f4c380dfca17.sourceText: Given the extensive coverage discussed above, this research contributes to addressing gaps in the landscape by:

0d643aac5cc26f1f0de13b4f34be5182416919ef.sourceText: Deconstructing monolithic narratives of Chinese identity by including diverse voices, particularly those of Hainanese women

507a7739461de0e70b60b9ef58578235b40c6483.sourceText: Prototyping innovative museum practices that enhance visitor engagement with textual artifacts

4058c2e6fcf1eae1591a7419597d765d963b6323.sourceText: Advancing theoretical understandings of embodied heritage engagement

88a91a7ac49bb6f5ed2599d415a331291553b9fb.sourceText: Singapore’s position as a multicultural society with significant Chinese diaspora populations offers a critical alternative to the PRC’s state-centered interpretations. As Frost (2003) argues, Singapore’s approach to Chinese heritage necessarily differs from mainland narratives, creating space for what Ang (2001) describes as the “impossible position” of diaspora communities—caught between essentialist notions of Chinese identity and their own complex, hybrid experiences. This research leverages Singapore’s unique cultural positioning to develop counter-narratives that deconstruct monolithic conceptions of “Chineseness” while creating new nexuses of connection.

61a0e8ea4e38a205d355c824027b3a346187e5a3.sourceText: The National Museum of Singapore operates within a multicultural national narrative that positions Chinese heritage as one component of a diverse society rather than as an extension of mainland Chinese nationhood. Such institutional positioning creates space for what Yeoh and Kong (2012) describe as “multivocal heritage interpretations” that recognise diverse perspectives within and across ethnic categories.

8edb875dabdbbb96f9a5cd5f2069f05626106bf0.sourceText: Within this context, Hainanese women’s correspondence represents voices subject to multiple layers of marginalisation. The Hainanese themselves were marginalised within broader Chinese society long before migration. Kiungchow (modern-day Haikou) was historically “an outpost where for over a thousand years Chinese officials were banished for offending their emperor” (Nield, 2015, p. 141). This profound geographical marginalisation shaped the island’s cultural and economic development, positioning it as peripheral to mainstream Chinese society.

864786b73274a5340059f3000e2daea49c18cb74.sourceText: In Singapore, the Hainanese faced additional layers of marginalisation. Arriving later than other dialect groups, they constituted only the fifth-largest Chinese dialect group (Conceicao, 2023). Their linguistic differences made communication with other Chinese communities difficult, as their dialect was largely unintelligible to Hokkien, Teochew, and Cantonese speakers. Economically marginalised, they were forced into service sectors like cooking and domestic work as more lucrative trades were already dominated by earlier Chinese migrants.

5c50a400fdf3a3278c28363a1e20eb4a5a3ad09a.sourceText: Hainanese women thus experienced at least three intersecting layers of marginalisation: as residents of a peripheral island historically used for political exile; as late-arriving migrants to Singapore with linguistic barriers; and as women within patriarchal structures that viewed female migration with suspicion. Their correspondence represents what Bhabha (1994) would describe as “border lives” at the intersection of multiple forms of marginality—experiences that profoundly challenge simplistic nationalist narratives centered on patriotic loyalty to the motherland.

b97605367a23c446eaeb242222c6d4a07ec0e822.sourceText: 1.6 The Challenge of Making Letters Accessible

9338dcdc6ebdd380f822c140dcd7e0061b5f523d.sourceText: Beyond the political dimensions of interpretation, Chinese diaspora correspondence presents significant practical challenges for contemporary museum display. As Serrell (2015) discusses, lengthy exhibit labels can lead to reduced visitor engagement in museum settings. This engagement challenge is particularly acute for materials written in classical Chinese or regional dialects, which remain inaccessible to many visitors including younger Singaporeans.

3e8e5d08e757ae50aca85e4ac6fa81ec13fa991f.sourceText: Traditional approaches to presenting historical correspondence—through translated displays, video recreations, or touchscreen interactives—frequently fail to create meaningful engagement with these materials. As Smith (2006) argues, heritage interpretations often impose fixed narratives that privilege curatorial authority over visitor meaning-making. Digital interfaces, while providing information access, often create what Parry (2010) describes as “informational rather than affective engagement” (p. 123)—privileging factual knowledge over emotional connection.

e399e295a0029811c849e6ad040fbf747536d0eb.sourceText: This recognition has led to our exploration of biometric approaches to visitor engagement—specifically, heart rate synchronisation as a means of creating embodied connections with historical materials. By translating the emotional content of letters into sound experiences that respond to visitors’ heart rates, we address both the political challenge of challenging nationalist narratives and the practical challenge of making these materials accessible to diverse visitors. This represents a first-of-its-kind presentation of

1be070b799aa73cb31d86834407a30cbca84d128.sourceText: 2. New Museology and Embodied Experience Applied

ef395571b56dc15c0e7b37dd1af7063e5e3facc4.sourceText: Our approach integrates new museology and embodied experience to create a coherent framework for understanding and engaging with marginalised diaspora correspondence. These interconnected perspectives inform both our analysis of letter content and our development of biometric engagement methods.

9c0e04d0e02975aa3bf4407d40e1e50ae92326ca.sourceText: As articulated by Hooper-Greenhill (2000), new museology questions authoritative curatorial voices and seeks more democratic, visitor-centred, and multivocal presentations of cultural artefacts. This theoretical framework positions museums not simply as repositories of objects but as sites of experience, meaning-making, and social engagement. Simon’s (2010) concept of the “participatory museum” also provides a particularly relevant framework for this research.

f13998e53a69b5bd4c1e400c5001e8bf22c01788.sourceText: Complementary to this is Gurian’s (2006) concept of “essential museums,” which emphasises that objects serve primarily as conduits for human connection and storytelling rather than as ends in themselves. This perspective is particularly valuable for text-heavy artefacts like letters, which derive their significance not from their material properties but from the human experiences and relationships they embody.

8661eac44d5bffb9254fce73dd4ebb8a689a0135.sourceText: The biometric application is also grounded in emerging scholarship on embodied knowledge and affective history. Crouch (2003) argues that bodily engagement transforms abstract knowledge into lived experience, creating deeper and more meaningful connections to cultural content. Similarly, Witcomb (2013) demonstrates how affective engagement in museum spaces can create stronger connections to historical materials than purely cognitive approaches. By synchronising visitors’ heart rates with soundscapes derived from letter content, the installation creates emotional and bodily connections that collapse temporal distance and foreground shared human experiences across historical contexts, aligning with Ahmed’s (2014) exploration of how emotions can bridge temporal and cultural divides. Tröndle and Tschacher’s (2012) research on “embodied resonance” between visitors and cultural artefacts supports our approach to creating affective connections through biometric synchronisation.

ad53f67cb961a401c9fb774e0a0d154bf652b7a3.sourceText: This integrated framework supports a multi-sensorial approach to heritage engagement where visitors “feel” their way into historical experiences that might otherwise remain inaccessible. By synchronising traditional percussion patterns to visitors’ heart rates, we create what Witcomb (2015) describes as a “pedagogy of feeling”—learning through emotional and bodily engagement rather than purely intellectual analysis. This approach addresses what she identifies as the challenge of creating “affective histories” that engage emotional and bodily responses alongside intellectual understanding.

385a487e534e652e7702193030053c1286c9ea13.sourceText: 3. Methodology: From Content to Experience - Letters, Heartbeats, and Sound

7bc59083480f066cc3d8b728b0dbe1bbf5d1f91f.sourceText: Having reviewed the corpus of relevant existing studies and areas in which this paper aims to contribute, the following section will detail how we arrive at the chosen letters, discuss further the value of heart rate synchronisation as well as the final prototype developed.

4b9d654c47ab5cb77b77876ae9137d2b8f84c832.sourceText: for analysis followed a multi-stage filtering process. Beginning with 2,265 items from the National Museum of Singapore’s collection containing the keyword “letter,” we excluded non-paper materials to reach 887 items. Further manual review identified 385 Chinese letters, from which we focused particularly on correspondence involving Hainanese women.

a52d88f52b4f60a980f4659d0418ed1ff165605f.sourceText: Our focus on Hainanese women’s letters was both incidental and deliberate. Incidental because these were among the few letters in the collection that featured a female sender or recipient, and deliberate in addressing significant gaps in existing research which has predominantly examined male-authored correspondence. It’s worth noting that some letters may have been written by professional letter writers rather than the stated senders themselves, as literacy rates were low, particularly among women. However, even professionally written letters would typically capture the sender’s intended messages and concerns, filtered though they might be through the scribe’s writing conventions.

9d340c33f257bbe63f66a8999da853f5483bf7ec.sourceText: Our analysis of Hainanese women’s letters reveals themes and concerns that are more quotidian than nationalistic. Two specific letters exemplify these counter-narratives:

a7c5da78ffaeb997c6794e4766856ac1c8db6a29.sourceText: Letter 1 · He Aifang to He Qinge

76f721ad6787ec0ce445775517b4e13cec37e096.sourceText: Letter from He Aifang (何爱芳) to He Qinge (何庆娥) in Haikou, Hainan, dated March 2, 1960. National Museum of Singapore, Accession No. 2000-06963-004, “Remittance letters delivered by Shun Chen Rong Remittance House.”

924388bec9a4890f9d855d6cda7cc2b474e19fa9.sourceText: Historical remittance letter from He Aifang to He Qinge, handwritten vertically in Chinese

5eb3e5a387ce8f831218689a100f75bdd318906b.sourceText: Letter 1. From He Aifang to He Qinge (March 2, 1960). Source: National Museum of Singapore, Accession No. 2000-06963-004.

b8f113275bfa1342948b5be12879a81f410b3484.sourceText: The letter acknowledges receipt of Hong Kong dollars and discusses the education of siblings—content that centres family relationships and educational planning rather than national allegiance.

df945744757ca5ffb543003cc0b4aab1b5eddb91.sourceText: Letter 2 · A mother in Hainan to Fu Zhifeng

0be854beefc0dc8ca333ba48d4bc3fd226ca984e.sourceText: Letter from a mother in Hainan to her son Fu Zhifeng (符致逢), dated March 10, 1954. National Museum of Singapore, Accession No. 2000-06965-002, “Letter to Fu Zhi Fong from mother in Hainan.”

0e9bc22c8f832277c82538341abf22c01ef2c83a.sourceText: Historical remittance letter from a mother in Hainan to Fu Zhifeng, handwritten vertically in Chinese

7b58fc46e3b8749aff39c6554023dc0958d2e0e7.sourceText: Letter 2. From a mother in Hainan to Fu Zhifeng (March 10, 1954). Source: National Museum of Singapore, Accession No. 2000-06965-002.

8c035ef6e5dfc1288b1bb722d0c757d04b9495c3.sourceText: The letter mentions receipt of Hong Kong dollars, discusses the mother’s health concerns, and requests a visit with tonics. The content centres intimate family relationships, bodily concerns, and practical matters rather than national or political themes.

ffcf2acdafe4c2c592a7ff383f2ca82304cbf6a6.sourceText: These letters reveal what Scott (1990) describes as “hidden transcripts”—perspectives and experiences that exist outside officially sanctioned narratives. These materials document everyday concerns, family relationships, and personal struggles that complicate nationalist framings emphasising patriotic loyalty. By centring these marginalised voices, we contribute to what Chakrabarty (2000) describes as “provincializing” dominant historical frameworks.

77ce651d2db8685bccaf853b5dee6a0bf125d8be.sourceText: The ordinary lives documented in Hainanese women’s letters hold profound significance for world history. As Hsu (2000) argues, diaspora correspondence provides “history from below” that reveals how global forces—colonialism, capitalism, and nation-building—were experienced, negotiated, and sometimes resisted by ordinary people. The use of Hong Kong dollars reflects how these women navigated complex currency regimes and financial networks established by colonial powers. Their concerns about health, education, and family well-being demonstrate how care economies functioned across transnational spaces, maintaining social cohesion despite geographic separation.

002aee8efc2c22521f2a4af46d04abc53f892aa1.sourceText: The heart rate provides a particularly appropriate biometric signal for connecting visitors to historical materials for several reasons:

909ed048eb7e8f3a55d6828088445ebf8e5188ab.sourceText: : Everyone has a heartbeat, creating a genuinely universal entry point to cultural materials that transcends linguistic, cultural, and educational differences.

bf90e0ae9cdf345b4d89b89a4e3a52784b80f9b1.sourceText: : The heartbeat carries powerful metaphorical associations with life, emotion, and human connection across most cultural traditions, making it an intuitive connector to historical materials about human relationships. Indeed, the heart is often metaphorically associated with emotions across cultures (Kövecses, 2000). The phrase “breathing life” into history becomes literal through this physiological connection.

7b94fe6b603c8e368262e3ae0dae4321ba9c48d0.sourceText: : Heart rate operates both below conscious control and within awareness, representing a form of what Nacke et al. (2011) term “implicit interaction” (p. 103)—physiological engagement that occurs without deliberate user actions. This characteristic makes heart rate potentially valuable for museum contexts where visitors may feel self-conscious about explicit interactive behaviors (Hornecker & Stifter, 2006, p. 138).

4c60c912cfb98c29e8317ee1ba40ee73bac849f3.sourceText: : This setup, where heart rate influences the soundscape and the soundscape may in turn affect the visitor’s physiological state, exemplifies a biofeedback loop, a concept well-established in physiological computing.

cc4c71d95ea7118e8f23a9fc23f4d0d223b1087a.sourceText: By using heart rate as the physiological bridge between visitor and historical material, we allow visitors to literally “feel” their way into someone else’s story, creating a multi-sensorial pathway to understanding that doesn’t require the ability to read classical Chinese.

1bc7bdbda870fd369c8cce06b3550406e0471e8a.sourceText: Our interactive prototype translates the emotional content of Hainanese women’s letters into sound experiences synchronised with visitors’ heart rates. The system architecture comprises primary components as detailed below:

05b0d560c85b0a05c85647576740a8170c9b94bd.sourceText: System architecture connecting a Bluetooth heart-rate monitor, emotional analysis, musical pattern generation, visual elements, and sound output

96ef0e9b1298da3c7d43fe062974b0e81b3c408b.sourceText: Figure 1. System diagram. Created by the author.

d2536f7afafb26bd65114b04ef889bb4ae12700e.sourceText: : The system takes real-time heart rate data from a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) device, using a mapping function that converts physiological heart rates (60-120 BPM) to musical tempos (65-95 BPM). This creates a direct connection between the visitor’s bodily state and the musical experience.

c3335124d075daab20dc312396876a353fecba15.sourceText: : Each letter has predefined emotional metrics capturing its content, including emotional intensity, urgency, and dominant emotions. These metrics are based on close textual analysis of the letters. The emotional analysis component translates these textual emotional dimensions into parameters for sound generation, facilitating a cross-modal mapping from text to sound, a process central to the field of affective computing (Picard, 1997).

a2ebf6fc71bb895430c8ad437d1536c1d16ab3f3.sourceText: : The system generates percussion patterns structured in three sections (entrance, emotional, and exit), creating a complete narrative arc for each letter. The patterns use traditional opera percussion instruments—Bangu (板鼓) as the main rhythmic instrument, Daluo (大锣) for accent points, Xiaoluo (小锣) for ornamental flourishes, and Naobo (铙钹) for punctuation . For the purpose of quick prototyping, the percussions were taken from this dataset of Beijing opera as it was readily available (Tian, Srinivasamurthy, Sandler, & Serra, 2014). This approach creates what Kirshenblatt-Gimblett (1998) describes as “cultural resonance”—connections between historical materials and their living cultural contexts. The interactive experience follows a structured flow with three distinct phases:

477ec60a53c7e0b1a6bf9f648d6f178e8b3c14aa.sourceText: : The experience begins with the gradual fade-in of visuals and simple rhythmic patterns as the visitor’s heart rate visualisation begins. This phase serves as a “scaffolded entry” that allows visitors to understand how their heart rate influences the experience before full engagement.

eb5728dc1aa2d6fc3c7b3e25f7fb018872f4b2ad.sourceText: : The core experience features the full letter reveal, complex pattern variations, and peak emotional expression. During this phase, the visitor’s heart rate directly influences the tempo and intensity of the percussion patterns, creating an “affective resonance” between visitor and historical material.

15c17827372c9d9c49131a1a1286369ff9631f47.sourceText: : The experience concludes with pattern simplification, visual fade-out, and gradual tempo reduction. This phase provides closure and reflection, embodying what Simon (2010) describes as the “me-to-we” design principle—moving from personal experience to broader social and historical connections.

2f586a73db8c33bdf60b67ff6be5121144cf2ab5.sourceText: This system creates a dynamic, responsive experience where the user’s heart rate influences both the musical and visual elements, while the emotional content of the letters provides the structural framework for the experience. The three-section structure (entrance, emotional, exit) ensures a complete narrative arc, while the real-time heart rate input keeps the experience personal and engaging.

3f755f402167e13ec4c92051f23c5d01086ad766.sourceText: This project demonstrates the practical application of key concepts from new museology. Its relevance to museum practice, in proposing counter-narratives and making visible marginalised voices will be discussed below.

34dc9e9e45511f61d90681eedb7bf5ded14a0382.sourceText: The findings from this research have significant implications for museum practice, particularly for the display and interpretation of text-heavy historical artefacts. Traditional approaches to exhibiting letters—displaying them under glass with accompanying explanatory text—can create significant barriers to engagement, particularly for items in languages unfamiliar to most visitors (Bitgood, 2013). The biometric approach demonstrates a viable alternative that can significantly increase both engagement duration and emotional connection with such materials.

d65c2fc271f40b966a09502326cb29a3dc40955b.sourceText: The biometric approach also offers practical solutions to engaging visitors across Singapore’s linguistically diverse population. By creating non-linguistic points of access to these materials, the installation enables meaningful engagement regardless of visitors’ fluency in Chinese dialects or Chinese writing, making these important historical materials accessible to all Singaporeans regardless of linguistic background.

67a34876085efe97c7f667723157e0ea172205b0.sourceText: For heritage institutions, particularly those in contexts like Singapore with complex relationships to larger nation-states like China, this research demonstrates practical approaches to developing counter-narratives that challenge dominant nationalist framings. By highlighting everyday concerns, women’s voices, and local contexts in the presentation of diaspora materials, museums can create more nuanced understandings of transnational experiences that resist subsumption under singular national narratives.

4914cd877df01823e7ab371f28ca531a2346a815.sourceText: This approach has particular relevance in contemporary contexts where heritage increasingly functions as a domain of soft power and cultural diplomacy. As Winter (2015) notes in his analysis of heritage diplomacy in Asia, cultural institutions often navigate complex geopolitical dynamics in their presentation of shared heritage. Singapore’s presentation of Chinese diaspora materials in ways that acknowledge connections to China while emphasising distinctive local developments represents an important model for balancing these considerations.

7e61f91041ae9a023a0c4f0dc14a1c2fada49e69.sourceText: Perhaps most significantly, this research offers practical mechanisms for amplifying historically marginalised voices. By making women’s letters—often overlooked in traditional scholarship—accessible and emotionally resonant for contemporary audiences, the project demonstrates how technological innovation can serve broader goals of inclusivity and diverse representation in cultural heritage. For the National Museum of Singapore specifically, this approach aligns with institutional commitments to representing the nation’s multicultural heritage and complex historical relationships.

244cf214441fb4f091b019f4d1ec03afb9b8d2ad.sourceText: In summary, “If Letters Home Could Sing” demonstrates how embodied heritage engagement can challenge nationalist narratives while making historically significant materials accessible to diverse audiences. For Singapore, this project represents an opportunity to deconstruct monolithic narratives of Chinese identity by including diverse voices, creating an alternative nexus of story that binds people together through shared human experience rather than national allegiance. By centring Hainanese women’s voices and developing innovative approaches to their presentation, Singapore’s heritage institutions can challenge the mono-narrative of patriotic loyalty to the motherland while affirming the global significance of ordinary lives that traversed national boundaries.

35e2922b1b2b059a1b8ff6039e1f46ece40885b4.sourceText: The methodology developed through this research demonstrates how embodied, physiological engagement can create meaningful connections with historically and linguistically complex materials. By literally allowing visitors to “breathe life” into historical letters through their heartbeats, we create possibilities for understanding the past not as a distant, fixed narrative but as a living presence that continues to resonate through our bodies and communities.

5f76d7ff7e1bf030a5b39877cbba6f9aafc84290.sourceText: Future directions for this research include expanding the methodology to other marginalised correspondence in museum collections, developing more sophisticated emotional mapping techniques, and conducting longitudinal studies of visitor engagement and learning outcomes. The prototype can also be developed further with more informed musical involvement and clan institutions.

e729c88f66d3603b58f250221383e27efdea474f.sourceText: As museums globally seek ways to remain relevant in an increasingly digital world, “If Letters Home Could Sing” offers a model that transcends the binary of technological innovation versus human experience. Indeed, this research suggests a way forward where museums become spaces not just for preserving the past, but for creating living connections between cultural heritage and contemporary experience – one heartbeat at a time.

b4d0bf3029c9cf2beff8a928bf4c24c6f06afc06.sourceText: This research was supported by the National Heritage Board through the National Museum of Singapore’s 2024 Research Fellowship programme. I extend my sincere gratitude to the curatorial team at the National Museum of Singapore for their invaluable guidance and for providing access to their rich collection of

57b66d38492e978ad42e99d889b24155b24aef99.sourceText: The opinions, findings, and recommendations expressed in this publication are those of the Research Fellow and do not necessarily reflect the views of the National Heritage Board.

c38af5531ea54cc4240634939e40c190e80d6163.sourceText: On a personal note, this research is deeply inspired by and dedicated to the incredible Hainanese women in my life—my late mother and grandmother—whose strength, resilience, and wisdom continue to influence me. It feels particularly meaningful that the letters I found most compelling were written by Hainanese women; I did not set out specifically to find these voices, but perhaps they found their way to me. By amplifying these historically marginalised voices, I hope to honour my family heritage while revealing how women’s everyday concerns formed the essential yet often unacknowledged foundation upon which strong, transnational communities were built and sustained.

Much of creative production is a grind of adaptation. Content changes.
        Collaborators bring different versions. Work moves between formats and
        audiences. Each change can mean repeating adjustments, reconstructing
        earlier choices and repairing their knock-on effects. The judgments that
        made a version work are buried in artifacts and editing histories,
        making them difficult to reuse, combine or revise independently.

In the proposed shared workflow, a model can make proposals while people

The evaluation will use matched tasks and a strong native workflow with
        the same content briefs, model access, and renderer. Its primary measure
        is total active editing time: capturing decisions, composing, adapting,
        checking, and repairing. The proposed initial target is at least 20%
        less active work, not an observed result. Secondary measures cover
        retained decisions, task completion, and blind output quality. A
        five-task pilot will precede a counterbalanced editor study.

b2a870694838b04a507777c65e27bea0426bbe5e.sourceText: Semantic Responsive Typesetting reverses that relationship: the document stays persistent; pages, columns, and line breaks are computed for a target.

99cc4b158cf3e9033689d62c31ba97c9de253544.sourceText: A canonical graph is combined with a target profile, a deterministic composition policy, and optional target-specific overrides. a3000c8c78b1d22d029f20bce2326b4c68de4268.sourceText: AI   is   fucking   everywhere:   at   work,   at   school,   in   our homes, in our phones, on our streets, in our governments, and at war. We are living through an era of extreme AI hype. In this climate, some people have gotten rich off of the   stolen   data   and   stolen   labor   that   fuels   these technologies.   Others   have   been   surveilled,   oppressed, exploited, and killed. This text presents a short, practical guide   to   the   technologies   currently   called   'AI,'   the ideologies   and   actors   pouring   gasoline   on   the   AI dumpsterfire, and what we can do about it.

9ef1ee5892e8d62801b8c197cb1ed381d616ff3e.sourceText: AI is a bunch of random tools. Some people describe these tools as 'human-like' in order to sell a product

da0ef22ab600bdb15432fd2ce87c24f2ed1bd5d8.sourceText: There's no such thing as 'AI' in the way the tech industry promotes it. AI is marketing hype, not 'intelligence.' What people call AI is a messy collection of tools that do stuff: ChatGPT extrudes   plausible-sounding   text,  Midjourney spits   out   synthetic   images,   Instagram's  algorithm sorts you into demographic categories to annoy you with ads, Amazon's  product recommendation system cyberstalks your every click to sell you stuff you don't need. We use scare quotes occasionally to remind you that 'Artificial Intelligence' is marketing hype and science fiction -

f78955047156a177ed23d47dd2adc89d642896f6.sourceText: Popular chatbot tools like ChatGPT produce

634e2a67cbe17eb010abae8af0659d74bb5494c4.sourceText: like   they   can   'think' 'understand' or 'reason.' They cannot. These models are trained on massive, uncurated datasets of text scraped from the web. All these 'Large Language Models' do is predict the next word in a sequence.  That's it. They're indifferent to truth and are better understood as either 'Bullshit Machines' [1] or 'Stochastic Parrots' [2].

3314a17e28411a657b7ac492e8f21e36a34802fd.sourceText: Comparing   AI tools to human   intelligence is anthropomorphization :   the   attribution   of   human traits to nonhuman things. People do this all the time and it's usually no big deal:

edade127cd0b8580210c64c632e6ad48d46ced15.sourceText: The title of this zine is of course tongue-in-cheek: 'AI' can only 'die' in the same sense that your cellphone 'dies.'

644d241e647722b7498f9ca3d1400ef7311330a2.sourceText: Problems arise when we get tricked into believing AI tools are a good stand-in for human behaviors: AI grifters are financially incentivized to overstate the ability of their tools to be our friends, lovers, therapists or replace us in the workforce. These sci-fi delusions are useful for selling people AI  products.   Despite   the   fact   that   'AI'   doesn't exist, it's ruining everything anyway [3].

e02e02282816f5df1019d31406bd3a416e0b8190.sourceText: AI hype cycles are periods in which attention and capital   gets   diverted   toward   whatever   random computing tools people are calling 'AI'

a3ae6b7933423f6849a7b27a0d1cb8bd9d00f65d.sourceText: The tools and technologies called 'AI' have gone through periods of popularity where they capture the attention of industry, science, and the general public. At other times called 'AI Winters' these tools have lost attention and become ordinary   parts   of   everyday   technology.   There have been two winters in the past. We're currently living in the third hype cycle.

e29359187b8aefef699469d6700b9c76426814d3.sourceText: In some eras AI was largely what we call statistics today. At   other   times   it   was   sprawling   logic   rule-sets   called 'expert systems.' In others it's been 'neural networks' or 'deep learning.' The technical details of these terms don't matter much for our purposes.

4a9707c7aa6f00a807b406ba9bcd9fa060306180.sourceText: The things we call 'AI' are a constantly rotating cast of half-working technologies.

e39561474736fd6fe80e06e95acbf25cfb9a5718.sourceText: When hype  for  AI   increases,   the   tools   and   methods labeled  AI   get   adopted   by   science,   industry,   and   the military. This leads to a positive feedback cycle: there's more   investment,   more   research,   and   more   products driving further hype. Eventually expectations exceed the ability of these technologies to deliver on their promises and the hype collapses. This leads to broad criticism and disillusionment with the field: an AI winter.

c7241aa6eae70e191f0e943fac93f1eefe3b9784.sourceText: AI technologies developed during a hype cycle eventually   become  'normal.'  They're   no longer considered AI and fade into the everyday. Nobody is bothered by the fact that their smartphone uses face detection when snapping a picture: this 'AI' tool is old news - the hype for this particular technology is over.

748898070c21a3e509086f129b887e0dc412e204.sourceText: Like AI, there are plenty of other tech products that go through hype cycles- and they don't necessarily provide any benefit to humanity.

d0368bb2339bdec152367b5a3c05d5609eedc44b.sourceText: As we're currently living in the third AI hype cycle, no one truly   knows   what   socially

7e18f4b782047b587d5d77f688866659606d1aa1.sourceText: technologies will stick around when the hype eventually blows over.

d383b2a38450a78ba8e53f22a3da34161c92c850.sourceText: 'Workers entered the field around 1950, and even around 1960, with high hopes that are very far from having been realized in 1972. In no part of the field have the discoveries made so far produced the major impact that was then promised.'

cb9c3fea5ef9c47a590070082cbdfd84e3c14ba9.sourceText: Now that we understand AI products are just hyped up tools, we need to recognize that

b1ad049b1f6675d5b20bc3ad0f38839b040013ac.sourceText: The real-life harms caused by AI technologies are well documented. These harms can't be addressed with more or 'better' technology - we need good oldfashioned social progress

bb586c66c20bd9d51a43fea341ba6cfa4ae8d6de.sourceText: The question of whether 'AI' causes harm has already been   answered:   harms   have   been   documented   by scientists, journalists, and scholars the world over. This section   is   a   rapid-fire   annotated   bibliography   of exceptional   scholarship   and   reporting   that   exposes various   kinds   of   automated   violence.   We   encourage curious   readers   to   follow   these

543893f75713deb10adb9ce5f64669f68192e8ba.sourceText: The   interdisciplinary   authors   of   'On   the   Dangers   of Stochastic Parrots: Can Language Models be Too Big? '   [3]   accurately   predicted  many of the environmental 🦜 and   social   harms   arising   from   the   broad   adoption   of 'stochastic   parrots':   a   pejorative   name   for   the   core technology   underlying   popular   chatbots   like   OpenAI's ChatGPT, Google's Gemini, Meta's Llama and X's Grok. Google tried to suppress the publication of the

845ba454782df75752de374597913ce23412f921.sourceText: s paper,   a   clear   example   of   scientific   research

7aec14843fec90527b69a0708ff542d02ecca160.sourceText: Mathematician and Data Scientist Cathy O'Neil illustrated how   unregulated   algorithmic   systems   perpetuate   and scale   discrimination   -   describing   AI   based   decision systems as 'Weapons of Math Destruction' [6].

d7fc683dede3cc32ffe02a7c5fefd9b80eddd60d.sourceText: The work of Computer Scientists Joy Buolamwini and Timnit Gebru analyzed how and why AI facial recognition systems discriminate based on skin color and gender [7].

c3b8662cd2519371b95bde37724af3908b08e9cf.sourceText: Scholar and activist Sasha Costanza-Chock demonstrated   how   TSA   body   imaging   machines disproportionally   flag   transgender   peoples'   bodies   for additional screening [8].

437a279bb75a951a4977fff60a284b64d6f40aa8.sourceText: 'Anomalies' detected by a TSA body scanner [7]

ff4795115d318d22442cd658f3da16486b4192c5.sourceText: Disability Studies and Tech Ethics scholar Ashley Shew has   highlighted   how   AI   products   reflect   an   implicitly ableist   design   philosophy   and   often   treat   individual experiences of disability as medical impairments rather than challenges arising from social barriers [9].

590ab2c6471c0003d00e1dfa307ffcdfd4e5c66b.sourceText: A   ProPublica   investigation   [10]   demonstrated   how algorithms that  detect   criminal   re-offense   entrench   the classist,   racist,   and   xenophobic   foundations   of   the criminal justice system.

371f5402ebc1d789fc2522c8ab12af75a30b771a.sourceText: Political Scientist Virgina Eubanks thoroughly documented the many ways in which algorithmic systems 'profile, police and punish the poor' [11].

08974f115107ee2e7ebb32a9b5eafeee2dba75ab.sourceText: ' Predictive   Policing'   algorithms,   intended   to   forecast crime (think of the movie

bd0ef1a3ae5091c9e2531ab869984e31ef3ac700.sourceText: Report ) , only serve to increase surveillance and oppression of poor communities [12], are racially biased, and notoriously bad at actually predicting crime [13].

c84c24af3b6437d8f7f44de161a51f1485674d1b.sourceText: Heat map of officer patrols in parts of Elgin, Illinois. Credit: Geolitica

8e874ab5d4a1f324826b0ffa90719c1fadce86bb.sourceText: Deepfake   tools   have   been   used   to   generate   nonconsensual pornography and revenge porn [14]. Some of the   datasets   that   these   AI   models   are   trained   off   of contain   hateful,   violent,   and   abusive   content   including Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) [15].

3a35c25f647272c15eb6f183516b8c70e0c0169d.sourceText: The Israeli military is field-testing 'robot dogs' in Gaza and has deployed a targeting system called "Habsora" ('The Gospel') to automate target selection for the IDF [16]. The world over, AI systems deployed by the military industrial complex   spy,   target,   and   murder   while   the   corporate developers of these technologies (from Lockheed and Raytheon to Palantir, Anduril,  and   OpenAI   [17,   18]   to Amazon [19] and Google [20]) reap massive profits from mass suffering and death.

12f4f52ecde0e1c23a8c0a7344d4b2a8e6f49335.sourceText: US Army Robot dog,Spc. Dean John Kd De Dios/DVIDS stopkillerrobots.org

f074ad4690bf313edb3045556d3f23ac10fdc3c6.sourceText: Automated violence arises from inequalities in who has the power to design and deploy AI systems. The largely homogenous groups of people developing, peddling, and profiting from AI do not care about the human beings their tools harm

eb2dff7e1328dfd4b492e44d766d5b2e9221b818.sourceText: Data Scientist Catherine D'Ignazio and Digital Humanities scholar Lauren F. Klein calls this inability of AI peddlers to understand   or   care   about   the   harmful   effects   of   their products  ' privilege

e88ed15fe80b02c7b7d39f78e6e79a40f8a6c920.sourceText: 'Those who occupy the most privileged positions among us-people with good educations, respected credentials, and professional accolades-are poorly equipped to recognize instances of oppression in the world'

e9f29559521ee5567e835d814d8df6d7fea0b12e.sourceText: ~You can't code your way out of a social problem ▊

e81e65106e5e22e4abeddac74d1f078fb6342ceb.sourceText: The ways that new technologies affect our lives is determined   by   who   has   ownership,   agency,   and power

b09a6e1b673b1ae49e2ab8416d691071a09cba78.sourceText: When the world is in an AI hype cycle, as it is now, new tools replace older tools because they're faster, cheaper, or simply more hyped up. The owners and creators of these tools get rich in the process, while others lose their jobs. There's nothing new about this process. New tools are developed, jobs change, and the relationship between workers and their work evolves as a result.

99fa5baf05cb516b6e612db2cb141fa12c625142.sourceText: What matters now is how society will respond to these technological changes: will power be further concentrated in the hands of the tech elite? Will union efforts suffer? Will workers get screwed?

a13111a95cb455c872417beac19841aee5424aa1.sourceText: "The AI can't do your job, but the AI salesman can convince your boss to fire you and replace you with an AI anyway"

aee8c73579645ea89168aca0356e5a544805bf51.sourceText: New weaving technologies were developed in the United Kingdom during the Industrial Revolution.   As   these   technologies   were   adopted   by factory owners, many workers took issue with the new machines disrupting their jobs.

0e80f23511801c5d16959ce730439320f5d2688f.sourceText: fought back by destroying these new machines.

6a3993a827fc5f4893621843363a5c4257533089.sourceText: While   Luddites   have   been   mischaracterized   as   being against all technology, they were in fact reacting to shitty working conditions where they were likely to be maimed or killed by the machines they worked with.

de13a7ea151070f3f738473c68be88a4c3409199.sourceText: Smashing looms was their tactic, not their goal

ce264283b0f22b16915564dffd39c917a5e870a2.sourceText: 1812 illustration of Luddites smashing a loom. (Chris Sunde / Wikimedia Commons)

ba63919e0badf8edc50501544933f5c278a0ba03.sourceText: Why do these algorithms create such absurd outcomes? [23] AI has politics [24, 25], and those politics are not neutral. Proponents of AI technology claim that with more of your data, AI tools will produce better outcomes. But who owns the data? Who gets to choose what tools get made from it? Who gets money and power when these tools are adopted by society? Who gets to decide what 'better' even means?

df0d0cf0548c25af41fe89392800728ef9e7b61f.sourceText: Consolidation   of   wealth   and   social   control   in   the hands   of   AI   authoritarians   are   features   of   these systems, not bugs .

6c15cca5f323649ec2c26d508e957cee7d8690ac.sourceText: This   way   of   thinking   refocuses   our   attention   on   the systems these tools are a part of, rather than the tools themselves. Like the Luddites, the problem is not the technology itself, but lack of ownership and control. Who has the power to decide what's designed, how it's built and how it's used?

fb1ab6b7ec70241bee9acb9aa26e37f5e0f353a1.sourceText: Tech   billionaires are   incentivized   to   support ideologies that emphasize tech's progress instead of social progress, as social progress can threaten their wealth and power

d8f367a9d1a4a7eb848885db775587de7d3f9521.sourceText: If you're a techie type you've probably seen people start companies, build cool new products and get rich. If you're interested   in   high   technology   and   enjoy   working   with these tools, you might be inclined to support the goals of your   company   and   be   skeptical   of   interference   and regulation   by   the   government. Libertarian ideologies might be very appealing to you: 'get the government out of my business and let me make the world a better place ' [26].   This   belief   system   follows   naturally   from technooptimism , the idea that we can create social progress by inventing new technologies that free people from their labors.

3f322f3653bd2868a124d5bb81a361766d650095.sourceText: ' Techno-optimism' is largely repackaged, sci-fi flavored reactionary politics. For instance, venture capitalist Marc Andreessen's   'Techno-Optimist   Manifesto'   is   no   more than old-school elitism for a techbro audience. In this unhinged, rambling text he vilifies ethicists, academics, regulators, and conservationists in a section titled 'The Enemy'. We invite the reader  to  find   and   read   it   for themselves - it's wild .

eef2195add81959f85e3e5ec1a45975f425adc43.sourceText: Techno-optimism doesn't offer the world anything more than unregulated capitalism, a worship of the rich, and the vague hope that the products and services they create will eventually,

7dc8a13ef7b3ee89a88797e0a42ff29ea5e01453.sourceText: please ,   solve our social ills, even though there's no evidence that technology  alone ever leads to social progress.

293c068a9183a6a15d633a64b6dd166ee2bce1b2.sourceText: Techbro   ideologies   are   zero-commitment   and   zeroaccountability - thin veils for the worship of their one true god: profit .

cf04a3a1fa918c2842b789a6bd4e7470b9e5f678.sourceText: Billionaires think the solutions to problems caused by billionaires are known only to billionaires.

40e43cf88dfd293d3f7b6ed9b44cc4a4879401c4.sourceText: as  revolutionizing   and transforming society for the better, that the human race is on the cusp of a utopian age of 'human flourishing' or 'abundance.' If you're a techno-optimist in the 2020s, the most   fantastical   way   to   do   this   is Artificial   General Intelligence (AGI).

03da9f2543aaf1565ff669d89de04b1c41768f47.sourceText: AGI is the hyped up idea that we're close to creating some kind of super 'AI agent' with human-like abilities across   a   wide   variety   of   domains.   Techno-optimists believe that AGI is good, controllable and imminent:

6e486a565f8be27ddbdff61efd5c2d7badc909bf.sourceText: for only $9.99 per month, everyone gets their own digital servant!

42c2c509e89dcc0a3024fbb740618700a3e943d8.sourceText: Not   all   discourse   around  AGI   is   framed   optimistically. 'Doomers'   claim   the   emergence   of   AGI   will   destroy humanity. This is termed 'existential risk' or 'x-risk.'

eebc69daf952278e6f8abf022ab8fbee451a3112.sourceText: However   both   AGI-optimist   and   AGI-doomer   ways   of thinking serve to perpetuate the AI hype cycle and shift focus away from the real harms of AI towards the fictional: sci-fi

90691b06e6ab8c1ee4313167fdaca356db710657.sourceText: scenarios or benevolent machine gods. Some even mix the two, claiming that AGI is inevitable and   beneficial,   but   anyone   who   resists   it   will   be retroactively punished by the AGI god ( see

118d0c5b09d83435bcfc124b2b30a497f55a0b7b.sourceText: We provide a short overview of these wacko ideas so you can better spot them in the wild (and avoid them). This clusterfuck of  AGI fantasies have come to be collectively referred to as the 'TESCREAL Bundle' [27].

eecec5154fc682daf54c2197cdc0ee7f0344322e.sourceText: This acronym, coined by Timnit Gebru and philosopher Émile P. Torres refers to:

9dee9f22acbbfa7fc0739325f51bcbabc7768ae9.sourceText: - the human body is weak and can be transcended with technology, somehow.

e0a8eea37273d95da365a9c6cd2a223cfd337127.sourceText: -   the   goal   of   life   is   to   reverse entropy   (impossible)   but   an   AGI   god   with superpowers can help us do that, hopefully.

6ebad50d9267abc260e4a049a9e83f68d5c435e8.sourceText: is nigh and AGI god will happen - trust us.

0921c6c09b4c2f06ccad2b712c320962af18cbd3.sourceText: This technical report introduces Docling , an easy to use, self-contained, MITlicensed open-source package for PDF document conversion. It is powered by state-of-the-art specialized AI models for layout analysis (DocLayNet) and table structure recognition (TableFormer), and runs efficiently on commodity hardware in a small resource budget. The code interface allows for easy extensibility and addition of new features and models.

f28c0804c4f50e33172447761795de2e3608d00f.sourceText: Converting PDF documents back into a machine-processable format has been a major challenge for decades due to their huge variability in formats, weak standardization and printing-optimized characteristic, which discards most structural features and metadata. With the advent of LLMs and popular application patterns such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), leveraging the rich content embedded in PDFs has become ever more relevant. In the past decade, several powerful document understanding solutions have emerged on the market, most of which are commercial software, cloud offerings [3] and most recently, multi-modal vision-language models. As of today, only a handful of open-source tools cover PDF conversion, leaving a significant feature and quality gap to proprietary solutions.

ae7da7633a2d40795fc2220bbfcee6ca84a19ff7.sourceText: With Docling , we open-source a very capable and efficient document conversion tool which builds on the powerful, specialized AI models and datasets for layout analysis and table structure recognition we developed and presented in the recent past [12, 13, 9]. Docling is designed as a simple, self-contained python library with permissive license, running entirely locally on commodity hardware. Its code architecture allows for easy extensibility and addition of new features and models.

7dfaa7dc2e43a81bff68e55159d36cc2546c5200.sourceText: Here is what Docling delivers today:

c36335cdd03ec0512757f8d52ccb7b3a81276930.sourceText: Converts PDF documents to JSON or Markdown format, stable and lightning fast

df6d2bb580f20c24a6a9f58a01015895a30a924d.sourceText: Understands detailed page layout, reading order, locates figures and recovers table structures

b77a8b2b64eb6b51a4da6ffb21ec95c3987fe544.sourceText: Extracts metadata from the document, such as title, authors, references and language

ee66a39080fb75921340483b68e90349ec53bd43.sourceText: Optionally applies OCR, e.g. for scanned PDFs

03a23dc04b2d6553afe0fcc6f33162f453cbe00e.sourceText: Can be configured to be optimal for batch-mode (i.e high throughput, low time-to-solution) or interactive mode (compromise on efficiency, low time-to-solution)

5ad4963973181cc5a6a48c01342690e8bac0d560.sourceText: Can leverage different accelerators (GPU, MPS, etc).

034c43d351a507f7d2bd3fc46e9e3a6982e55599.sourceText: To use Docling, you can simply install the

1238eb8f507f18b8dc41851dc3441daa5b459037.sourceText: package from PyPI. Documentation and examples are available in our

2582fe886b9f5544cbad286c0ca32205d11e4a2c.sourceText: are downloaded to a local huggingface datasets cache on first use, unless you choose to pre-install the model assets in advance.

7a18cf9456826687e986706b09681cd5baf08f83.sourceText: Docling provides an easy code interface to convert PDF documents from file system, URLs or binary streams, and retrieve the output in either JSON or Markdown format. For convenience, separate methods are offered to convert single documents or batches of documents. A basic usage example is illustrated below. Further examples are available in the Doclign code repository.

1bacd387c3797f3a92e4797e8b03aa1e2078ddde.sourceText: Optionally, you can configure custom pipeline features and runtime options, such as turning on or off features (e.g. OCR, table structure recognition), enforcing limits on the input document size, and defining the budget of CPU threads. Advanced usage examples and options are documented in the README file. Docling also provides a

6ee63b079f8e577d8992a65ad05cc8a1c12b2d72.sourceText: to demonstrate how to install and run it inside a container.

8d2163ae076ea260345432726ed83d1e2ab729a0.sourceText: Docling implements a linear pipeline of operations, which execute sequentially on each given document (see Fig. 1). Each document is first parsed by a PDF backend, which retrieves the programmatic text tokens, consisting of string content and its coordinates on the page, and also renders a bitmap image of each page to support downstream operations. Then, the standard model pipeline applies a sequence of AI models independently on every page in the document to extract features and content, such as layout and table structures. Finally, the results from all pages are aggregated and passed through a post-processing stage, which augments metadata, detects the document language, infers reading-order and eventually assembles a typed document object which can be serialized to JSON or Markdown.

4bc145294ba709fb8e2b4fd758362bd80b9e2963.sourceText: Two basic requirements to process PDF documents in our pipeline are a) to retrieve all text content and their geometric coordinates on each page and b) to render the visual representation of each page as it would appear in a PDF viewer. Both these requirements are encapsulated in Docling's PDF backend interface. While there are several open-source PDF parsing libraries available for python, we faced major obstacles with all of them for different reasons, among which were restrictive licensing (e.g. pymupdf [7]), poor speed or unrecoverable quality issues, such as merged text cells across far-apart text tokens or table columns (pypdfium, PyPDF) [15, 14].

8c3800ab5d56f4033a3c89d5f01e960623e7544e.sourceText: Figure 1: Sketch of Docling's default processing pipeline. The inner part of the model pipeline is easily customizable and extensible.

9d105e8ee93bf118c00d78cf9718c887a5f84cd3.sourceText: We therefore decided to provide multiple backend choices, and additionally open-source a custombuilt PDF parser, which is based on the low-level qpdf [4] library. It is made available in a separate package named

eaa74dd7d33c5987eb39923b5b3295f1a0a524fa.sourceText: and powers the default PDF backend in Docling. As an alternative, we provide a PDF backend relying on pypdfium , which may be a safe backup choice in certain cases, e.g. if issues are seen with particular font encodings.

a57bc7a41b53083a8523de9447e38092ed6f06d3.sourceText: As part of Docling, we initially release two highly capable AI models to the open-source community, which have been developed and published recently by our team. The first model is a layout analysis model, an accurate object-detector for page elements [13]. The second model is TableFormer [12, 9], a state-of-the-art table structure recognition model. We provide the pre-trained weights (hosted on

712c4ed949ee6516f4f897d815e446e33ea706b4.sourceText: and a separate package for the inference code as

b088bffc2dafe7e6fa9b589c926e44aa58a28c97.sourceText: . Both models are also powering the open-access

eaf6f5122072dcd69ee18069a806d5604ecf0c7c.sourceText: , our cloud-native service for knowledge exploration tasks.

ff486a03c14d8c5123382431dfad45fb2d660730.sourceText: Our layout analysis model is an object-detector which predicts the bounding-boxes and classes of various elements on the image of a given page. Its architecture is derived from RT-DETR [16] and re-trained on DocLayNet [13], our popular human-annotated dataset for document-layout analysis, among other proprietary datasets. For inference, our implementation relies on the

00c3c73e493d2758b902cd535e71249acaf194e0.sourceText: The Docling pipeline feeds page images at 72 dpi resolution, which can be processed on a single CPU with sub-second latency. All predicted bounding-box proposals for document elements are post-processed to remove overlapping proposals based on confidence and size, and then intersected with the text tokens in the PDF to group them into meaningful and complete units such as paragraphs, section titles, list items, captions, figures or tables.

8663b76e20df9043c4ab33689621763684eece84.sourceText: The TableFormer model [12], first published in 2022 and since refined with a custom structure token language [9], is a vision-transformer model for table structure recovery. It can predict the logical row and column structure of a given table based on an input image, and determine which table cells belong to column headers, row headers or the table body. Compared to earlier approaches, TableFormer handles many characteristics of tables, such as partial or no borderlines, empty cells, rows or columns, cell spans and hierarchy both on column-heading or row-heading level, tables with inconsistent indentation or alignment and other complexities. For inference, our implementation relies on

f0386468402be34392929caaa70365c27551a6de.sourceText: The Docling pipeline feeds all table objects detected in the layout analysis to the TableFormer model, by providing an image-crop of the table and the included text cells. TableFormer structure predictions are matched back to the PDF cells in post-processing to avoid expensive re-transcription text in the table image. Typical tables require between 2 and 6 seconds to be processed on a standard CPU, strongly depending on the amount of included table cells.

f19201cba60b3393ff0c217230bc39833fcff37e.sourceText: Docling provides optional support for OCR, for example to cover scanned PDFs or content in bitmaps images embedded on a page. In our initial release, we rely on

8d11b0ca9aa3a958a3c3da345063793294b77104.sourceText: [1], a popular thirdparty OCR library with support for many languages. Docling, by default, feeds a high-resolution page image (216 dpi) to the OCR engine, to allow capturing small print detail in decent quality. While EasyOCR delivers reasonable transcription quality, we observe that it runs fairly slow on CPU (upwards of 30 seconds per page).

41e8242718f1fc356885c52416c54a99d43427c0.sourceText: We are actively seeking collaboration from the open-source community to extend Docling with additional OCR backends and speed improvements.

6c5bb0febc7c5dda1001f7d4ad77550f1aa2907d.sourceText: In the final pipeline stage, Docling assembles all prediction results produced on each page into a well-defined datatype that encapsulates a converted document, as defined in the auxiliary package

46322b3161138f26122ffd48f35d770d363e155e.sourceText: . The generated document object is passed through a post-processing model which leverages several algorithms to augment features, such as detection of the document language, correcting the reading order, matching figures with captions and labelling metadata such as title, authors and references. The final output can then be serialized to JSON or transformed into a Markdown representation at the users request.

76fae28ef3c499c67d8db18f9bc7729f7cc30b5f.sourceText: Docling provides a straight-forward interface to extend its capabilities, namely the model pipeline. A model pipeline constitutes the central part in the processing, following initial document parsing and preceding output assembly, and can be fully customized by sub-classing from an abstract baseclass ( BaseModelPipeline ) or cloning the default model pipeline. This effectively allows to fully customize the chain of models, add or replace models, and introduce additional pipeline configuration parameters. To use a custom model pipeline, the custom pipeline class to instantiate can be provided as an argument to the main document conversion methods. We invite everyone in the community to propose additional or alternative models and improvements.

02ab6e38b71efab869eb2e0278c391bca4614a92.sourceText: Implementations of model classes must satisfy the python Callable interface. The __call__ method must accept an iterator over page objects, and produce another iterator over the page objects which were augmented with the additional features predicted by the model, by extending the provided PagePredictions data model accordingly.

37f2b25294a6ce71a2b11db9a06fe690a05c8a8a.sourceText: In this section, we establish some reference numbers for the processing speed of Docling and the resource budget it requires. All tests in this section are run with default options on our standard test set distributed with Docling, which consists of three papers from arXiv and two IBM Redbooks, with a total of 225 pages. Measurements were taken using both available PDF backends on two different hardware systems: one MacBook Pro M3 Max, and one bare-metal server running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS on an Intel Xeon E5-2690 CPU. For reproducibility, we fixed the thread budget (through setting

2228294bbbef19a07918dd66189de1e7420fede1.sourceText: variable ) once to 4 (Docling default) and once to 16 (equal to full core count on the test hardware). All results are shown in Table 1.

595e07f5623f193045afe9fcd95730ca9a6d00e0.sourceText: If you need to run Docling in very low-resource environments, please consider configuring the pypdfium backend. While it is faster and more memory efficient than the default

47933f4d72f07b6d6bace436a7170f86642cea7c.sourceText: backend, it will come at the expense of worse quality results, especially in table structure recovery.

7e29a86bcf213989bed675e4ff1f6f4b26244546.sourceText: Establishing GPU acceleration support for the AI models is currently work-in-progress and largely untested, but may work implicitly when CUDA is available and discovered by the onnxruntime and torch runtimes backing the Docling pipeline. We will deliver updates on this topic at in a future version of this report.

8cd9283c5b547e4067416e0f1432da55099d000b.sourceText: Table 1: Runtime characteristics of Docling with the standard model pipeline and settings, on our test dataset of 225 pages, on two different systems. OCR is disabled. We show the time-to-solution (TTS), computed throughput in pages per second, and the peak memory used (resident set size) for both the Docling-native PDF backend and for the pypdfium backend, using 4 and 16 threads.

cc6f073c0fcba9bbcb3747c04436cee1e0952138.sourceText: Thanks to the high-quality, richly structured document conversion achieved by Docling, its output qualifies for numerous downstream applications. For example, Docling can provide a base for detailed enterprise document search, passage retrieval or classification use-cases, or support knowledge extraction pipelines, allowing specific treatment of different structures in the document, such as tables, figures, section structure or references. For popular generative AI application patterns, such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), we provide

8ea6b80037b410e91f5d6ce0c02b76b6fa3a7153.sourceText: , an open-source package which capitalizes on Docling's feature-rich document output to enable document-native optimized vector embedding and chunking. It plugs in seamlessly with LLM frameworks such as LlamaIndex [8]. Since Docling is fast, stable and cheap to run, it also makes for an excellent choice to build document-derived datasets. With its powerful table structure recognition, it provides significant benefit to automated knowledge-base construction [11, 10]. Docling is also integrated within the open IBM data prep kit [6], which implements scalable data transforms to build large-scale multi-modal training datasets.

47d3825b6c63e3a667b036ab288f4b5805e9529d.sourceText: Docling is designed to allow easy extension of the model library and pipelines. In the future, we plan to extend Docling with several more models, such as a figure-classifier model, an equationrecognition model, a code-recognition model and more. This will help improve the quality of conversion for specific types of content, as well as augment extracted document metadata with additional information. Further investment into testing and optimizing GPU acceleration as well as improving the Docling-native PDF backend are on our roadmap, too.

a7a1c7806a3ff65ce47e5daa5974ee9943d7c0fe.sourceText: We encourage everyone to propose or implement additional features and models, and will gladly take your inputs and contributions under review . The codebase of Docling is open for use and contribution, under the MIT license agreement and in alignment with our contributing guidelines included in the Docling repository. If you use Docling in your projects, please consider citing this technical report.

Much of creative production is a grind of adaptation. Content changes.
        Collaborators bring different versions. Work moves between formats and
        audiences. Each change can mean repeating adjustments, reconstructing
        earlier choices, and repairing their knock-on effects.

27cbd6bfce8a3977e029ad28459f2e5d991b1dab.sourceText:
Workflows built around sequential edits make these operations cumbersome
        and repetitive. The judgments behind the work remain difficult to
        isolate, reuse or revise.

05352ed603abd7fe2faf06bc4d415529fd63df4b.sourceText:
Develop software that represents content, creative decisions and their
        dependencies as explicit, editable structures. A decision records what
        it applies to, its scope, the conditions under which it remains valid,
        and its relationships to other decisions. The model is extensible with
        new decision types and operations.

7063bd6efff9a9b759e363a5da9bde56c4c60b73.sourceText:
supplies the document layer: structured
        content, assets, relationships, and reading renditions. The decision layer
        is application-owned and proposed; it does not make Struct responsible for
        creative policy or revisions. It is not a universal Struct schema or a competing
        canonical editorial store.

14c8a4ce65541a20680b60176a50385bde560a9e.sourceText:
A bounded, application-owned source of truth for content, creative
          decisions, and dependencies supports parallel branches and forms
          derived for different contexts.

1029b369519dc66ce6a33cd0923551cba90861cb.sourceText:
A typed API would apply operations with preconditions, validity checks,
        and conflict diagnostics. People and agents can then share a state,
        develop variants independently, combine accepted decisions, and check
        what remains applicable after change.

Matched tasks will compare this workflow with a strong native workflow
        using the same content briefs, model access, and renderer. The primary
        measure is total active editing time: capture, composition, adaptation,
        checking, and repair. The proposed initial target is at least 20% less
        active work, with retained decisions, completion, and blind output
        quality as secondary measures. A five-task pilot precedes a
        counterbalanced editor study.

bf0f2c5dec3398620d66e8897a40235d01769a60.sourceText:
Replay, branching, and remixing existed before large language models.
        Autonomous creative work now needs explicit shared state, accepted
        decisions, and dependencies so people and agents can inspect, combine,
        and check changes. REPResenting Taste investigates those foundations.
