s0194.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > h1 > h1

s0195.sourceText: This project demonstrates the practical application of key concepts from new museology. Its relevance to museum practice, in proposing counter-narratives and making visible marginalised voices will be discussed below.
s0195.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > p > p

s0196.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > section > h2 > h2

s0197.sourceText: The findings from this research have significant implications for museum practice, particularly for the display and interpretation of text-heavy historical artefacts. Traditional approaches to exhibiting letters—displaying them under glass with accompanying explanatory text—can create significant barriers to engagement, particularly for items in languages unfamiliar to most visitors (Bitgood, 2013). The biometric approach demonstrates a viable alternative that can significantly increase both engagement duration and emotional connection with such materials.
s0197.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > section > p > p

s0198.sourceText: The biometric approach also offers practical solutions to engaging visitors across Singapore’s linguistically diverse population. By creating non-linguistic points of access to these materials, the installation enables meaningful engagement regardless of visitors’ fluency in Chinese dialects or Chinese writing, making these important historical materials accessible to all Singaporeans regardless of linguistic background.
s0198.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > section > p > p

s0199.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > section > h2 > h2

s0200.sourceText: For heritage institutions, particularly those in contexts like Singapore with complex relationships to larger nation-states like China, this research demonstrates practical approaches to developing counter-narratives that challenge dominant nationalist framings. By highlighting everyday concerns, women’s voices, and local contexts in the presentation of diaspora materials, museums can create more nuanced understandings of transnational experiences that resist subsumption under singular national narratives.
s0200.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > section > p > p

s0201.sourceText: This approach has particular relevance in contemporary contexts where heritage increasingly functions as a domain of soft power and cultural diplomacy. As Winter (2015) notes in his analysis of heritage diplomacy in Asia, cultural institutions often navigate complex geopolitical dynamics in their presentation of shared heritage. Singapore’s presentation of Chinese diaspora materials in ways that acknowledge connections to China while emphasising distinctive local developments represents an important model for balancing these considerations.
s0201.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > section > p > p

s0202.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > section > h2 > h2

s0203.sourceText: Perhaps most significantly, this research offers practical mechanisms for amplifying historically marginalised voices. By making women’s letters—often overlooked in traditional scholarship—accessible and emotionally resonant for contemporary audiences, the project demonstrates how technological innovation can serve broader goals of inclusivity and diverse representation in cultural heritage. For the National Museum of Singapore specifically, this approach aligns with institutional commitments to representing the nation’s multicultural heritage and complex historical relationships.
s0203.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > section > p > p

s0204.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > h1 > h1

s0205.sourceText: In summary, “If Letters Home Could Sing” demonstrates how embodied heritage engagement can challenge nationalist narratives while making historically significant materials accessible to diverse audiences. For Singapore, this project represents an opportunity to deconstruct monolithic narratives of Chinese identity by including diverse voices, creating an alternative nexus of story that binds people together through shared human experience rather than national allegiance. By centring Hainanese women’s voices and developing innovative approaches to their presentation, Singapore’s heritage institutions can challenge the mono-narrative of patriotic loyalty to the motherland while affirming the global significance of ordinary lives that traversed national boundaries.
s0205.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > p > p

s0206.sourceText: The methodology developed through this research demonstrates how embodied, physiological engagement can create meaningful connections with historically and linguistically complex materials. By literally allowing visitors to “breathe life” into historical letters through their heartbeats, we create possibilities for understanding the past not as a distant, fixed narrative but as a living presence that continues to resonate through our bodies and communities.
s0206.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > p > p

s0207.sourceText: Future directions for this research include expanding the methodology to other marginalised correspondence in museum collections, developing more sophisticated emotional mapping techniques, and conducting longitudinal studies of visitor engagement and learning outcomes. The prototype can also be developed further with more informed musical involvement and clan institutions.
s0207.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > p > p

s0208.sourceText: As museums globally seek ways to remain relevant in an increasingly digital world, “If Letters Home Could Sing” offers a model that transcends the binary of technological innovation versus human experience. Indeed, this research suggests a way forward where museums become spaces not just for preserving the past, but for creating living connections between cultural heritage and contemporary experience – one heartbeat at a time.
s0208.context: html > body > div > main > div > article > div > div > div > section > p > p

s0215.sourceText: On a personal note, this research is deeply inspired by and dedicated to the incredible Hainanese women in my life—my late mother and grandmother—whose strength, resilience, and wisdom continue to influence me. It feels particularly meaningful that the letters I found most compelling were written by Hainanese women; I did not set out specifically to find these voices, but perhaps they found their way to me. By amplifying these historically marginalised voices, I hope to honour my family heritage while revealing how women’s everyday concerns formed the essential yet often unacknowledged foundation upon which strong, transnational communities were built and sustained.

s0028.sourceText:
Much of creative production is a grind of adaptation. Content changes.
        Collaborators bring different versions. Work moves between formats and
        audiences. Each change can mean repeating adjustments, reconstructing
        earlier choices, and repairing their knock-on effects.
s0028.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > p

s0029.sourceText:
Workflows built around sequential edits make these operations cumbersome
        and repetitive. The judgments behind the work remain difficult to
        isolate, reuse or revise.

s0031.sourceText:
Develop software that represents content, creative decisions and their
        dependencies as explicit, editable structures. A decision records what
        it applies to, its scope, the conditions under which it remains valid,
        and its relationships to other decisions. The model is extensible with
        new decision types and operations.

        is application-owned and proposed; it does not make Struct responsible for
        creative policy or revisions. It is not a universal Struct schema or a competing
        canonical editorial store.

s0056.sourceText:
Matched tasks will compare this workflow with a strong native workflow
        using the same content briefs, model access, and renderer. The primary
        measure is total active editing time: capture, composition, adaptation,
        checking, and repair. The proposed initial target is at least 20% less
        active work, with retained decisions, completion, and blind output
        quality as secondary measures. A five-task pilot precedes a
        counterbalanced editor study.

s0058.sourceText:

        Autonomous creative work now needs explicit shared state, accepted
        decisions, and dependencies so people and agents can inspect, combine,
        and check changes. REPResenting Taste investigates those foundations.

s0037.sourceText: How can we reconstruct scholarly documents for different reading surfaces and verify what survives, what changes, and what still needs correction?
s0037.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > p

s0038.sourceText:
The proposition is that the document remains a semantic graph. Pages,
        columns, and line breaks are renditions computed for a reading surface.
        Stable object identities connect headings, prose, figures, captions,
        references, and annotations across those renditions.
s0038.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > p

s0039.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > h2 > h2

s0040.sourceText:
The October 2026 proposal is a reproducible fidelity evaluation loop:
        compare version-matched PDFs and source HTML with generated Struct,
        XHTML, and EPUB; keep text flow, figures, tables, equations, references,
        and navigation separately accountable; and record localized regressions
        across reading profiles.
s0040.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > p

s0041.sourceText:
The adapter is available as an experimental converter. The unified
        comparison harness, independently adjudicated challenge corpus, and
        visual-fidelity work are proposals in progress. A successful conversion,
        a valid EPUB, or a model score alone does not establish faithful
        reconstruction.
s0041.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > p

s0053.sourceText:
Struct supplies a source-neutral document model, validation, and
        deterministic XHTML and reflowable EPUB rendering. Its reference PDF
        adapter uses Docling and PDF text, glyph, and link evidence to
        reconstruct a document before rendering. PDF reconstruction and semantic
        rendering are separate steps: a valid output file can still contain
        extraction errors.
s0053.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > p

s0054.sourceText:
The public demo exposes the reference PDF-to-EPUB path. The broader
        research also considers finite-height composition, source provenance,
        reader position, and annotation preservation. Trying the converter does
        not establish that all of those hypotheses have been evaluated.
s0054.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > p

s0055.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > h2 > h2

s0056.sourceText:
The September adapter work reported 155 of 156 papers passing its
        applicable source-derived reader checks across four local corpora. That
        is a historical implementation report, not independent validation of
        visual fidelity; the original reports were local artifacts and the
        proposed unified harness remains separate.
s0056.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > p

s0057.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > a > a

s0058.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > p

one trusted structured fixture with 11 nodes, one relationship, and
          two annotations
s0059.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > strong > strong

s0060.sourceText:
, across mobile, Paper Pro Move, Paper Pro, and print profiles. It
        recorded preservation of the supplied structure, relationship,
        annotations, and anchors, with no detected clipping or overlap in that
        fixture.
s0060.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > p

s0061.sourceText:
These are fixture-level engineering checks, not a corpus result or
        reader study. The recorded timings measure local composition after
        module initialization, not PDF extraction or end-to-end conversion
        latency.
s0061.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > p

        documents remained

s0070.sourceText:
The proposal investigates an integrated system for faithful composition
        across heterogeneous reading surfaces. Adaptive layout, PDF reflow, and
        annotation anchoring each have substantial prior art. The literature
        review is a targeted scoping review, prepared in July 2026, rather than
        a systematic review or proof of novelty.
s0070.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > p

s0075.sourceText:
Complex tables, equations, reading order, scans, and figure-caption
        associations can require correction or fall back to image regions.
        Automated checks do not replace comparison with the original source.
        Outputs from the demo are for review, rather than automatically approved
        publications.
s0075.context: html > body > div > main > div > div > p > p

s0076.sourceText:
Further work needs independent source truth, comparisons with relevant
        baselines, varied document and device evidence, and reader evaluation.
        The package and public publishing lifecycle remain development work;
        this page does not claim a registry release or a peer-reviewed result.
